newsitem.title: USA: Calif. man wins reprieve hours before execution.
newsitem.headline: Calif. man wins reprieve hours before execution.

text.p: A federal appeals court on Sunday threw out the death sentence of a California man convicted of a 1981 rape and murder less than 48 hours before he was due to be executed.

In a decision that set off a firestorm of controversy, an 11-judge panel of the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeal voted 7-4 to annul Thomas Thompson's death sentence and ordered that he receive a new trial on the rape conviction.
The judges also asked a U.S. district court to decide whether Thompson's first-degree murder conviction should stand in light of its ruling on the rape conviction.

Thompson, 42, had been scheduled to die by lethal injection at San Quentin State Prison near San Francisco soon after midnight on Monday for the 1981 rape and murder of Ginger Fleischli, 20, in Laguna Beach, southern California.

Thompson, who would have been the fifth person put to death in California since the state resumed executions in 1992, maintained he was innocent, and his attorneys fought a long battle to save his life. Death penalty opponents also took up the case.

Gregory Long, one of Thompson's attorneys, said he was very pleased with the appeals court decision. "We came perilously close to executing a man who is probably innocent of all of these crimes," he told Reuters.
Defence lawyers said Thompson was relieved and excited about the news.

Rob Stutzman, a spokesman for California Attorney-General Dan Lungren, called the decision shocking and said the state would immediately appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court on the grounds that the appeals court had abused its discretion.
"We believe this cuts against the very nature of the death penalty reforms that were enacted by the Congress and the president a year ago to prevent these types of successive appeals," he said.
A spokesman for Gov. Pete Wilson, who rejected Thompson's plea for clemency last week, said: "We are troubled by the court's decision."
Even if the Supreme Court reverses the decision, defence lawyers said it was unlikely the execution would go ahead as previously scheduled.

The appeals court panel said in a written ruling released in San Francisco that it was throwing out the death sentence and ordering a new trial on Thompson's rape conviction because of errors by Thompson's attorney at his 1983 trial.
The jury's finding that Thompson was guilty of murder with the "special circumstance" of rape made him eligible for the death penalty.
The court criticised Thompson's trial attorney Ronald Brower for not cross-examining the coroner about bruises on Fleischli's body that the coroner said could indicate rape.
It also lashed out at Brower for failing to attack more aggressively the credibility of two jailhouse informants who said that Thompson had admitted the crimes to them.

"Brower's cumulative errors in failing to investigate and impeach the jailhouse informants and to rebut the forensic evidence of rape cast grave doubt on the reliability of the rape conviction and the rape special circumstance finding and thus of the death sentence itself," the judges wrote.
The judges also said that the prosecution's use of conflicting theories of the murder in the separate trials of Thompson and his co-defendant David Leitch violated Thompson's right to due process.

The panel agreed with a district court judge who found in 1995 that Thompson's trial attorney "provided constitutionally deficient representation ..." But the district court was later overruled by a smaller panel of the appeals court which reinstated Thompson's death sentence.
The murder took place in the early hours of Sept. 12, 1981. After an evening of drinking and smoking hashish, Thompson returned to his Laguna Beach apartment with Fleischli.

Fleischli's body was found three days later in a shallow grave near a freeway. She had been stabbed five times in the head. Her shirt and bra had been cut in front and pulled down to her elbows. Investigators found her blood in the apartment. Thompson was convicted of rape and first-degree murder.
Leitch, Thompson's roommate, was convicted of second-degree murder for helping to dispose of the body and was sentenced to 15 years to life in prison.

Thompson maintained that he and Fleischli had consensual sex, after which he passed out. Thompson's lawyers said there was new evidence to support this, citing a statement by Leitch at a 1995 parole hearing that he came into the apartment and saw two people having sex.
